subject: ela
name: Academic Discourse Rubric
problemType: Inconsistent expectations for participation quality
targetMisconception: Speaking grades are subjective or based on frequency
teacherMoves: Provide ongoing feedback aligned to rubric
fadePlan: Teacher-created rubric ‚Üí co-created ‚Üí student-refined/self-assessed.
whenNotToUse: At the very beginning of the year before norms exist.

subject: ela
name: Academic Language Functions Toolkit (Argue‚ÄìExplain‚ÄìCompare‚ÄìEvaluate)
problemType: Lack of function-specific phrases for academic moves
targetMisconception: Academic English is just sounding formal
teacherMoves: Introduce four functions with L1/English examples (UDL 2.1)
Model choosing the right function for task/audience (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Bilingual frames ‚Üí English starters ‚Üí independent phrasing demonstrating function.
whenNotToUse: When creative writing intentionally departs from academic register.
formativeChecks: - Quick check: circle function used and highlight signaling phrase
Quick check: Identify which function you used and why.

subject: ela
name: Academic Language Scaffolding System
problemType: Students struggle with academic register and discourse
targetMisconception: Belief that academic language is arbitrary rather than serving specific purposes
teacherMoves: Teach academic language functions and purposes (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide scaffolds for academic language production (UDL 5.3)
Connect to professional and academic purposes (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Identify academic language demands of tasks
Use sentence frames for academic functions
Practice academic register in speaking and writing
fadePlan: Phase 1: Full sentence frame support for all functions → Phase 2: Reduced support with frame access → Phase 3: Independent academic language → Phase 4: Flexible academic register use
whenNotToUse: When informal language is appropriate for purpose or audience.

subject: ela
name: Accessibility Toolkit Introduction
problemType: Lack of awareness of assistive supports
targetMisconception: Assistive tools are only for IEPs
fadePlan: Teacher demos ‚Üí student tutorials ‚Üí independent selection.
whenNotToUse: When tech infrastructure is unstable.
formativeChecks: - Survey usage frequency and benefit statements
Self-report: Identify the tool you found most helpful and why.

subject: ela
name: Active Listening Log
problemType: Students tune out peers or fail to respond meaningfully
targetMisconception: Listening means waiting to speak
fadePlan: Full prompts ‚Üí stems only ‚Üí independent active listening.
whenNotToUse: When discussion is purely brainstorming and informal.

subject: ela
name: Anticipation Guide (Agree/Disagree)
problemType: Limited background knowledge and weak purpose-setting before reading
targetMisconception: Belief that reading begins only at the first line of the text, without activating prior knowledge or setting a purpose
teacherMoves: Model how to take a stance and justify with personal/community connections (UDL 7.2)
Read statements aloud and clarify vocabulary
Require students to revisit stances after reading and cite line numbers (UDL 6.3)
studentTasks: Take positions on 6‚Äì8 statements and explain why
Revisit stances after reading with textual evidence
fadePlan: Teacher models with full stems ‚Üí stems reduced ‚Üí no stems; students cite lines independently.
whenNotToUse: When texts are noncontroversial or topic could cause harm without agreements.
formativeChecks: - Collect guides and check for evidence-linked revisions
- 2-sentence exit: How did your stance change and why?

subject: ela
name: Argument Outline Tree (Claim‚ÜíEvidence‚ÜíCounterclaim)
problemType: Disorganized essay structure
targetMisconception: Arguments develop linearly without counterclaims
teacherMoves: Think-aloud how counterarguments reinforce claims (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Teacher-modeled ‚Üí guided ‚Üí independent outlines.
whenNotToUse: For short responses (<150 words) or informal discussions.

subject: ela
name: Argument Rebuttal Roundtable
problemType: Students state claims but struggle to refute equitably
targetMisconception: Refutation is about winning, not truth-building
fadePlan: Teacher-facilitated ‚Üí student-moderated ‚Üí independent debate writing.
whenNotToUse: When topic is personally sensitive and needs structured dialogue first.
formativeChecks: - Peer rubric for evidence quality + tone
Reflection: Describe how listening influenced your argument.

subject: ela
name: Argument Rubric Self-Assessment
problemType: Students cannot judge their own progress on criteria
targetMisconception: Grades are arbitrary rather than criteria-based
teacherMoves: Require cited evidence for each row
fadePlan: Teacher-facilitated scoring ‚Üí paired scoring ‚Üí independent reflection.
whenNotToUse: When rubric criteria are brand new and unfamiliar.

subject: ela
name: Argument Writing Structure and Strategy
problemType: Students write opinions without argumentative structure
targetMisconception: Belief that strong feelings make strong arguments
teacherMoves: Teach argument structure: claim, evidence, reasoning, counterclaim, rebuttal (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models complete argument structure → Phase 2: Guided component practice → Phase 3: Independent argument writing → Phase 4: Natural argumentative writing
whenNotToUse: When personal or creative expression is the goal rather than persuasion.

subject: ela
name: Author's Purpose and Craft Analysis
problemType: Students don't consider why authors make specific choices
targetMisconception: Belief that reading is about understanding what happened not why it's written that way
teacherMoves: Teach author's purpose analysis as reading skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model asking why questions about authorial choices (UDL 6.1)
Practice identifying techniques and analyzing effects (UDL 6.2)
Connect purpose to audience and context (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Identify author's overall purpose for text
Explain effect of techniques on reader
Connect techniques to purpose and audience
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models purpose and craft analysis → Phase 2: Guided analysis with prompts → Phase 3: Independent craft analysis → Phase 4: Automatic craft-conscious reading
whenNotToUse: When focus is on comprehension rather than craft analysis.

subject: ela
name: Student-Created Bilingual Glossary Builders
problemType: No access to disciplinary vocabulary in students‚Äô languages
targetMisconception: Glossaries must be monolingual teacher-made
fadePlan: Teacher starter terms ‚Üí student-added ‚Üí independent digital glossary.
whenNotToUse: When class time is extremely limited.
formativeChecks: Mini quiz: Define one term in both languages.

subject: ela
name: Bilingual Sentence Frames for Academic Register
problemType: Lack of academic argument language
targetMisconception: Home language must be suppressed to learn English
fadePlan: Full bilingual frames ‚Üí starters ‚Üí independent phrasing.
whenNotToUse: When students already show full register control.
formativeChecks: - Track frame use and accuracy of academic terms
Self-check: Provide one original academic sentence without using the frames.

subject: ela
name: Claim‚ÄìEvidence‚ÄìReasoning (CER) Paragraph Frame
problemType: Students present opinions without evidence or reasoning
targetMisconception: Evidence speaks for itself and needs no explanation
teacherMoves: Highlight transitions linking claim‚Üíevidence‚Üíreasoning (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Use color key to check balance
fadePlan: Full frame ‚Üí transitional prompts only ‚Üí student-generated CER without templates.
whenNotToUse: If students already master structured argument paragraphs or in creative writing tasks.

subject: ela
name: Character Arc Timeline
problemType: Identifying traits but not development
targetMisconception: Characters are static/defined by one label
teacherMoves: Tie change to conflict resolution (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Modeled ‚Üí guided ‚Üí independent.
whenNotToUse: When characters are symbolic rather than dynamic.

subject: ela
name: Character Motivation and Change Chart
problemType: Flat characters with unclear motives
targetMisconception: Characters 'just act' without needs or internal conflicts
teacherMoves: Connect motives to theme (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Guided charting ‚Üí independent tracking ‚Üí implicit integration.
whenNotToUse: When writing experimental fiction focused on style over character.
formativeChecks: evaluate cause‚Äìeffect reasoning for character motivation
Exit check: Explain one character‚Äôs motivation shift.

subject: ela
name: Character Analysis and Characterization Study
problemType: Students describe characters without analyzing how they're developed
targetMisconception: Belief that characters are fixed rather than developed through techniques
teacherMoves: Connect characterization to theme and purpose (UDL 7.2)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models with explicit technique identification → Phase 2: Guided character analysis → Phase 3: Independent character interpretation → Phase 4: Sophisticated character analysis
whenNotToUse: When character description rather than analysis is the goal.

subject: ela
name: Choice Reading Pathways
problemType: Low reading engagement and limited autonomy
targetMisconception: Only teacher-assigned texts count
teacherMoves: Model selecting by interest/challenge (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Teacher-curated ‚Üí student-suggested ‚Üí independent selection.
whenNotToUse: When a shared anchor text is required for common assessment.
formativeChecks: - Collect rationale entries and interest reflections
Reflection: Rate your choice‚Äôs difficulty and interest level.

subject: ela
name: Close Reading Multi-Pass Protocol
problemType: Students read texts superficially without deep comprehension
targetMisconception: Belief that understanding is achieved in one reading
teacherMoves: Teach close reading as multiple purposeful reads (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model each reading pass with different focus (UDL 6.1)
Provide annotation strategies for each pass (UDL 3.3)
studentTasks: Complete first read for gist understanding
Second read for key details and structure
Third read for analysis of craft and meaning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models each pass with shared text → Phase 2: Guided practice with structured passes → Phase 3: Independent multi-pass reading → Phase 4: Automatic close reading habits
whenNotToUse: When quick reading for main idea is appropriate or when text is below challenge level.

subject: ela
name: Code-Switching Mini-Lesson on Audience and Purpose
problemType: Difficulty adjusting register across contexts
targetMisconception: Formal English is superior to community dialects
studentTasks: Rewrite short text for new audience
fadePlan: Guided modeling ‚Üí collaborative rewriting ‚Üí independent application.
whenNotToUse: When identity judgments not yet safely discussed.
formativeChecks: Check: Identify how your register changed for a different audience.

subject: ela
name: Community Critical Inquiry Project
problemType: Students don‚Äôt apply literacy to real contexts
targetMisconception: ELA stops at analysis, not civic action
fadePlan: Teacher-scaffolded inquiry ‚Üí student-led teams ‚Üí independent capstones.
whenNotToUse: When local topics require prior approval and it‚Äôs not obtained.
formativeChecks: - Milestone checks on sources and audience analysis
Progress check: Note one source you evaluated for credibility.

subject: ela
name: Community Issue Editorials
problemType: Students don‚Äôt see writing as social action
targetMisconception: Writing is only for grades, not impact
fadePlan: Teacher-curated topics ‚Üí student-chosen ‚Üí independent publication.
whenNotToUse: When issues are sensitive and require prior consultation.
formativeChecks: - Check claim‚Äìevidence alignment for the target audience
Exit check: Provide one counterargument you considered.

subject: ela
name: Community Reader Showcase
problemType: No authentic recognition for reading growth
targetMisconception: Achievement exists only through tests/grades
teacherMoves: Coach presentation of favorite texts (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Teacher-run showcase ‚Üí student-led planning.
whenNotToUse: When community involvement logistics are infeasible.
formativeChecks: - Post-event reflection on motivation and identity
Audience survey: Rate how the presentation influenced your reading interest.

subject: ela
name: Comparative Literary Analysis Matrix
problemType: Generalized similarities; missing nuanced contrasts
targetMisconception: Comparison equals surface-level likeness only
teacherMoves: Show how contrast builds argument (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Fill matrix with evidence from both texts
fadePlan: Guided template ‚Üí self-created categories ‚Üí independent synthesis.
whenNotToUse: When analyzing only one text or during timed tests.

subject: ela
name: Comparative Literature Analysis Skills
problemType: Students don't effectively compare texts
targetMisconception: Belief that comparison means listing parallel features
teacherMoves: Teach comparative analysis as interpretive tool (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Develop comparison criteria based on analytical purpose
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models comparative analysis with criteria → Phase 2: Guided comparison with support → Phase 3: Independent comparative analysis → Phase 4: Natural comparative reading
whenNotToUse: When single text depth is the priority.

subject: ela
name: Writing Conference Checklist
problemType: Lack of focused feedback during conferences
targetMisconception: Conferencing is about editing rather than growth
teacherMoves: Guide students to lead part of the conference
fadePlan: Teacher-led ‚Üí student-led with checklist ‚Üí independent peer conferences.
whenNotToUse: During timed/high-stakes tests where conferencing disrupts pacing.

subject: ela
name: Context Clues Types Chart
problemType: Difficulty inferring word meaning from context in complex sentences
targetMisconception: Thinking unfamiliar words must always be looked up rather than deduced from context
teacherMoves: Teach four clue types with think-alouds (UDL 3.1)
Co-analyze sentences and label the clue type (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Prompt students to cite words that signaled meaning (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Infer meanings and record evidence phrases
fadePlan: Start with labeled examples and stems ‚Üí remove labels, keep list ‚Üí infer without lists and justify evidence.
whenNotToUse: If vocabulary is domain-specific and requires preteaching rather than context inference.

subject: ela
name: Critical Media Literacy and Analysis
problemType: Students consume media without critical analysis
targetMisconception: Belief that media is just entertainment without requiring analysis
teacherMoves: Teach media analysis as literacy skill (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with variety of media forms (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Analyze media texts using literacy frameworks
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models critical media analysis → Phase 2: Guided analysis with variety → Phase 3: Independent critical media consumption → Phase 4: Critical media literacy identity
whenNotToUse: When media is being used purely for content rather than media literacy.

subject: ela
name: Cross-Disciplinary Literacy Links
problemType: ELA strategies don‚Äôt transfer to other classes
targetMisconception: ELA strategies only apply in English
teacherMoves: Model disciplinary text strategies (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Apply ELA annotation/evidence in another subject
fadePlan: Teacher collaboration ‚Üí student recognition ‚Üí independent transfer.
whenNotToUse: When cross-curricular scheduling isn‚Äôt feasible.
formativeChecks: - Collect reflections showing concrete transfer links
Exit reflection: Describe how ELA strategies helped in another class.

subject: ela
name: Cross-Text Comparison Matrix
problemType: Weak comparative analysis between sources
targetMisconception: Comparing texts means listing similarities only
teacherMoves: Model matrix with themes and contrasts (UDL 3.2)
Highlight how differences build argument (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Peer revise for clarity and evidence
fadePlan: Full template ‚Üí partial ‚Üí student-made chart categories.
whenNotToUse: When analyzing a single text.
formativeChecks: - Check each column includes both texts and at least one contrast
Exit ticket: Write one contrasting theme with evidence from both texts.

subject: ela
name: Cultural Critique Panel Discussion
problemType: Texts analyzed without connection to current issues
targetMisconception: ELA analysis must be apolitical
studentTasks: Serve on a panel and cite evidence
fadePlan: Teacher-moderated ‚Üí student-moderated ‚Üí peer-planned panels.
whenNotToUse: When sensitive topics lack preparation and norms.
formativeChecks: - Panel rubric + self-evaluations on evidence and tone
Peer evaluation: Assess whether evidence used was relevant and respectful.

subject: ela
name: Culturally Relevant Text Connections Organizer
problemType: Students can‚Äôt see relevance in canonical texts
targetMisconception: Classic literature is universally applicable
fadePlan: Teacher-paired ‚Üí student-chosen pairings.
whenNotToUse: When time doesn‚Äôt permit two-text study.
formativeChecks: Short exit: Share one way the canonical text connects to your community.

subject: ela
name: Debate Evidence Tracker
problemType: Unsupported claims in academic debate
targetMisconception: Performance style outweighs reasoning
teacherMoves: Assign evidence manager role (HLP Cooperative Learning)
fadePlan: Scaffolded roles ‚Üí shared management ‚Üí self-tracking evidence.
whenNotToUse: When debates are informal/creative without factual grounding.
formativeChecks: - Spot-check logs for accuracy and balance
Mini quiz: Identify two strong pieces of evidence used in the debate.

subject: ela
name: Dialogue Punctuation Station
problemType: Confusion over dialogue formatting and speaker tags
targetMisconception: Punctuation rules don‚Äôt apply to creative writing
teacherMoves: Use sentence strips for kinesthetic practice
fadePlan: Guided strip practice ‚Üí independent editing ‚Üí implicit application in drafts.
whenNotToUse: When focus is content rather than conventions.

subject: ela
name: Differentiated Reading Pathways
problemType: Mixed readiness frustrates whole-class reading
targetMisconception: All must read same text at same pace
teacherMoves: Offer leveled options around shared theme (HLP Differentiated Support)
fadePlan: Teacher-assigned levels ‚Üí student-selected difficulty.
whenNotToUse: During standardized assessments requiring uniform material.
formativeChecks: Exit question: Compare your group‚Äôs theme interpretation with another group‚Äôs.

subject: ela
name: Digital Discussion Forum Scaffold
problemType: Shallow/off-topic online responses
targetMisconception: Digital replies don‚Äôt need evidence or tone awareness
fadePlan: Template ‚Üí checklist only ‚Üí student-created norms.
whenNotToUse: When platform access/moderation isn‚Äôt equitable.
formativeChecks: - Random audit for tone, evidence, engagement
Self-assessment: Rate your post for evidence use and respectful tone.

subject: ela
name: Disability Representation in Literature Analysis
problemType: Students encounter stereotypical or absent disability representation in texts
targetMisconception: Belief that disability stories must be inspirational or tragic
teacherMoves: Teach frameworks for analyzing representation quality (UDL 3.2)
Provide examples of authentic vs stereotypical portrayals (HLP Exemplars)
studentTasks: Identify disability representation in assigned text
fadePlan: Teacher-guided analysis → Partner analysis → Independent critical reading
whenNotToUse: When students have not yet established respectful discussion norms

subject: ela
name: Discussion Reflection Journal
problemType: Students don‚Äôt internalize feedback from class discussions
targetMisconception: Discussion ends when talk stops
teacherMoves: Provide guiding questions linking talk to text (UDL 5.3)
studentTasks: Set discussion goals for next session
fadePlan: Guided prompts ‚Üí partial prompts ‚Üí student-generated questions.
whenNotToUse: When multiple reflections already assigned that week (fatigue).

subject: ela
name: Literature Discussion and Seminar Skills
problemType: Students don't engage in substantive text-based discussion
targetMisconception: Belief that discussion is about stating opinions rather than exploring text
teacherMoves: Teach discussion as collaborative meaning-making (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Prepare for discussion with textual annotations and questions
Contribute ideas grounded in text evidence
Build on others' ideas rather than just adding
Ask genuine questions to deepen understanding
Reflect on discussion quality and learning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher facilitates with explicit move modeling → Phase 2: Shared facilitation with coaching → Phase 3: Student-led discussion → Phase 4: Natural discussion habits
whenNotToUse: When quick check of understanding is needed rather than extended discussion.

subject: ela
name: Diverse Voices and Perspectives in Literature
problemType: Literature curriculum excludes diverse voices and experiences
targetMisconception: Belief that literary canon is neutral and includes all worthy literature
teacherMoves: Intentionally include diverse authors and perspectives (UDL 7.3)
Teach literature as reflecting and shaping culture (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Support critical examination of whose voices are centered (UDL 3.2)
Connect to students' identities and experiences (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Read works by authors from diverse backgrounds
Analyze how identity shapes literary voice and perspective
Examine whose stories are told and whose are excluded
Connect literature to own identity and experience
supports: Diverse author/text bank organized by identity (UDL 7.3)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides diverse texts and guides analysis → Phase 2: Student exploration with guidance → Phase 3: Independent diverse reading and analysis → Phase 4: Ongoing diverse reading identity
whenNotToUse: Never - diverse voices should be central to all ELA instruction. Adjust texts to context.

subject: ela
name: Drama Text and Performance Integration
problemType: Students don't understand drama as performance text
targetMisconception: Belief that drama is read like prose rather than imagined as performance
teacherMoves: Teach drama as performance-oriented text (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model reading drama with performance imagination (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Analyze how staging choices affect meaning
Connect text analysis to performance possibilities
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models performance-oriented reading → Phase 2: Guided staging analysis → Phase 3: Independent interpretation and performance → Phase 4: Natural drama literacy
whenNotToUse: When reading drama for plot or theme without performance focus.

subject: ela
name: Grammar in Context and Meaning-Making
problemType: Students see grammar as arbitrary rules divorced from meaning
targetMisconception: Belief that grammar is about right and wrong rather than effective communication
teacherMoves: Teach grammar as meaning-making tool (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model how grammar choices affect meaning and style (UDL 6.1)
Practice grammar in authentic writing contexts (UDL 8.3)
Connect to reading and writing purposes (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Analyze how grammar affects meaning in mentor texts
Practice targeted grammar skills in context
Apply grammar learning to own writing
Edit own work for grammar and effect
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models grammar-meaning connections → Phase 2: Guided grammar analysis and practice → Phase 3: Independent grammar application → Phase 4: Natural grammar sense
whenNotToUse: When decontextualized grammar practice is appropriate for specific skill building.

subject: ela
name: Home Language Valorization and Translanguaging
problemType: Multilingual students' home languages are devalued in ELA
targetMisconception: Belief that English-only is appropriate for English class
teacherMoves: Allow translanguaging for thinking and processing (UDL 5.3)
Explore how languages work together (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Use home language for processing and brainstorming
Reflect on linguistic identity and growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher explicitly validates and models home language use → Phase 2: Structured translanguaging opportunities → Phase 3: Natural translanguaging with awareness → Phase 4: Confident multilingual identity
whenNotToUse: Never - home language should always be valued. Adjust visibility and structure as appropriate.

subject: ela
name: Informational Text Analysis and Evaluation
problemType: Students read informational text uncritically or avoid it entirely
targetMisconception: Belief that informational text is neutral or less interesting than fiction
teacherMoves: Teach informational text as constructed and purposeful (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model critical reading of informational texts (UDL 6.1)
Practice with variety of informational forms (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Identify author's purpose and perspective in informational text
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models critical informational reading → Phase 2: Guided analysis with variety → Phase 3: Independent critical reading → Phase 4: Critical informational literacy
whenNotToUse: When information is being used for content rather than literacy skills.

subject: ela
name: LGBTQ+ Inclusive Text Selection and Discussion Guide
problemType: Students rarely see LGBTQ+ experiences reflected in classroom texts
targetMisconception: Belief that LGBTQ+ topics don't belong in academic settings
teacherMoves: Curate diverse text sets including LGBTQ+ voices (UDL 7.2)
Establish discussion norms for identity conversations (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Engage with LGBTQ+ authored or themed text
Connect themes to universal human experiences
fadePlan: Teacher-selected texts → Student-recommended additions → Student-curated collections
whenNotToUse: When community context requires prior relationship building and norm setting

subject: ela
name: Active Listening Comprehension Development
problemType: Students passively listen without active comprehension strategies
targetMisconception: Belief that listening just happens without active effort
teacherMoves: Teach listening as active comprehension process (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model note-taking and questioning during listening (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Use active listening strategies during spoken text
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models with explicit strategies → Phase 2: Guided listening practice → Phase 3: Independent listening with strategies → Phase 4: Automatic active listening
whenNotToUse: When focus is on speaking or interactive conversation rather than extended listening.

subject: ela
name: Literary Analysis Essay Development
problemType: Students summarize plot rather than analyze literary techniques
targetMisconception: Belief that writing about literature means retelling the story
teacherMoves: Teach analysis as distinct from summary (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model developing analytical thesis about literary elements (UDL 6.1)
Practice body paragraphs that analyze rather than summarize (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Develop analytical thesis about author's craft
Build body paragraphs with analysis not summary
Use evidence to support analytical claims
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models analytical thinking and writing → Phase 2: Guided paragraph practice → Phase 3: Independent essay writing → Phase 4: Natural analytical approach
whenNotToUse: When personal response or creative writing is the goal.

subject: ela
name: Multimodal Composition and Digital Literacy
problemType: Students only compose in traditional text formats
targetMisconception: Belief that legitimate writing is only print text
teacherMoves: Teach multimodal composition as legitimate literacy (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Connect multimodal skills to communication purposes (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Analyze how modes work together in texts
Select modes appropriate for purpose and audience
Develop technical skills for multimodal creation
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher introduces modes and guides creation → Phase 2: Supported multimodal projects → Phase 3: Independent multimodal composition → Phase 4: Natural multimodal literacy
whenNotToUse: When traditional text composition is the specific learning goal.

subject: ela
name: Narrative Writing Skill Development
problemType: Students tell rather than show in narrative writing
targetMisconception: Belief that narrative writing is just recounting events
teacherMoves: Teach narrative craft techniques explicitly (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model show don't tell with before/after examples (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Develop narrative arc with conflict and resolution
Use sensory details to create imagery
Develop characters through action and dialogue
supports: Show don't tell examples and practice (UDL 6.1)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models each technique → Phase 2: Focused technique practice → Phase 3: Complete narrative writing → Phase 4: Natural narrative craft
whenNotToUse: When informational or argumentative writing is the focus.

subject: ela
name: Peer Review Skill Development
problemType: Students give vague or unhelpful peer feedback
targetMisconception: Belief that nice comments are more important than useful feedback
teacherMoves: Teach specific peer review skills (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Review peer work using specific criteria
Prioritize and apply feedback to revision
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models and monitors feedback → Phase 2: Structured peer review with coaching → Phase 3: Independent peer review → Phase 4: Natural peer feedback culture
whenNotToUse: When relationship isn't established or when peer feedback might be harmful.

subject: ela
name: Authentic Personal Narrative Development
problemType: Students don't see their stories as worthy of telling
targetMisconception: Belief that only dramatic or unusual experiences make good narratives
teacherMoves: Validate all student experiences as narrative-worthy (UDL 7.3)
Teach personal narrative craft (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Create safe space for story sharing (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Identify personal experiences worthy of narrative
Use craft techniques to tell story effectively
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher validates experiences and guides selection → Phase 2: Craft instruction with practice → Phase 3: Independent narrative development → Phase 4: Storyteller identity
whenNotToUse: When personal narrative might surface trauma without proper support.

subject: ela
name: Plain Language Translation Practice
problemType: Students struggle to communicate complex ideas clearly to diverse audiences
targetMisconception: Belief that academic language is always superior to plain language
teacherMoves: Model translating jargon to accessible language (UDL 3.1)
studentTasks: Identify jargon and complex structures in text
Verify clarity with peer from target audience
fadePlan: Teacher modeling → Collaborative translation → Independent plain language writing
whenNotToUse: When demonstrating mastery of academic register is the learning goal

subject: ela
name: Poetry Appreciation and Analysis Development
problemType: Students feel intimidated by or disconnected from poetry
targetMisconception: Belief that poetry is only for certain people or has one right interpretation
teacherMoves: Demystify poetry and validate multiple interpretations (UDL 7.3)
Teach poetry analysis strategies accessibly (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide diverse poetry including contemporary and culturally relevant (UDL 7.3)
Connect poetry to emotion and experience (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Read and respond to diverse poetry
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models accessible poetry engagement → Phase 2: Supported analysis and response → Phase 3: Independent poetry reading and writing → Phase 4: Poetry appreciation identity
whenNotToUse: When poetry analysis might reinforce intimidation rather than accessibility.

subject: ela
name: Reader Identity Affirmation and Development
problemType: Students don't see themselves as readers
targetMisconception: Belief that reading identity is fixed and can't be developed
teacherMoves: Create community around reading (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Connect reading to student interests and identities (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Explore personal reading history and preferences
Set personal reading goals aligned with interests
Engage in sustained reading with choice
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher creates reading community with choice → Phase 2: Supported reader identity development → Phase 3: Independent reading life → Phase 4: Lifelong reader identity
whenNotToUse: Never - reader identity should be developed continuously. Adjust choice and support levels.

subject: ela
name: Reading Comprehension Monitoring Strategy
problemType: Students continue reading even when comprehension breaks down
targetMisconception: Belief that finishing the reading is more important than understanding
teacherMoves: Teach comprehension monitoring as active reading (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Apply fix-up strategies: reread, slow down, question, connect
Reflect on reading process and growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher prompts monitoring at intervals → Phase 2: Self-prompted monitoring with support → Phase 3: Independent monitoring → Phase 4: Automatic monitoring habit
whenNotToUse: Never - comprehension monitoring benefits all reading. Adjust frequency and support.

subject: ela
name: Reading Goal Setting and Growth Tracking
problemType: Students don't set or track reading goals
targetMisconception: Belief that reading growth just happens without intentional effort
teacherMoves: Teach reading goal setting with growth mindset (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Help students identify reading growth areas (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Assess current reading strengths and growth areas
Select strategies to support goal attainment
Adjust goals and strategies based on progress
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides goal setting with assessment → Phase 2: Supported strategy selection and tracking → Phase 3: Independent goal management → Phase 4: Ongoing reading growth habits
whenNotToUse: When reading is purely for enjoyment with no skill focus.

subject: ela
name: Reading Group Collaboration Skills
problemType: Students don't learn effectively in reading groups
targetMisconception: Belief that reading is solitary rather than social
teacherMoves: Teach reading group collaboration skills (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Build from group to independent application (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Prepare for group discussion with text annotations and questions
Reflect on group effectiveness and learning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher structures groups with explicit roles → Phase 2: Reduced scaffolding with accountability → Phase 3: Student-organized groups → Phase 4: Natural collaborative reading
whenNotToUse: When individual reading assessment is needed.

subject: ela
name: Research Process Scaffolding System
problemType: Students don't follow effective research process
targetMisconception: Belief that research means finding sources that say what you want
teacherMoves: Teach research as inquiry process (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model question development and source seeking (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Evaluate sources for reliability and bias
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides each research step → Phase 2: Structured research with check-ins → Phase 3: Independent research with support → Phase 4: Natural research habits
whenNotToUse: When quick information-finding is needed rather than extended research.

subject: ela
name: Deep Revision Strategy Development
problemType: Students revise only for surface errors not content
targetMisconception: Belief that revision means editing for spelling and grammar
teacherMoves: Teach revision as rethinking not just editing (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model substantive revision with before/after examples (UDL 6.1)
Separate revision from editing in process (UDL 6.2)
studentTasks: Revise for global concerns: thesis, organization, development
Revise for paragraph-level concerns: coherence, transitions
Save editing for after content revision
Use revision strategies matched to identified needs
supports: Revision levels guide: global, paragraph, sentence (UDL 3.3)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides revision with explicit modeling → Phase 2: Structured revision with feedback → Phase 3: Independent revision with self-assessment → Phase 4: Natural deep revision habits
whenNotToUse: When writing is informal or when time doesn't allow for revision process.

subject: ela
name: Rhetorical Analysis Framework Development
problemType: Students don't analyze how texts persuade
targetMisconception: Belief that persuasion is about manipulation rather than rhetoric
teacherMoves: Teach rhetorical situation and strategies (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with variety of rhetorical texts (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Analyze rhetorical situation: author, audience, purpose, context
Apply rhetorical awareness to own writing
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models rhetorical analysis → Phase 2: Guided analysis with variety → Phase 3: Independent rhetorical analysis → Phase 4: Rhetorical awareness in reading and writing
whenNotToUse: When text is being read for content rather than persuasion.

subject: ela
name: Sentence Variety and Fluency Development
problemType: Students write with repetitive sentence structures
targetMisconception: Belief that sentence structure doesn't affect writing quality
teacherMoves: Teach sentence variety as stylistic tool (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice varying sentence beginnings, lengths, and structures (UDL 8.3)
Read aloud to hear rhythm and flow (UDL 6.4)
studentTasks: Analyze sentence variety in model texts
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models sentence manipulation → Phase 2: Focused sentence variety practice → Phase 3: Application to own writing → Phase 4: Natural sentence variety habits
whenNotToUse: When focus is on generating ideas rather than craft.

subject: ela
name: Literature and Social Issues Connection
problemType: Students don't connect literature to contemporary social issues
targetMisconception: Belief that literature is separate from real-world concerns
teacherMoves: Connect literature to contemporary issues intentionally (UDL 7.2)
Teach critical reading for social themes (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Support discussion of difficult topics safely (UDL 8.3)
Move from analysis to possible action (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Identify social issues in literature being studied
Connect literary treatment to contemporary manifestations
Analyze how literature illuminates social dynamics
Discuss issues with civil discourse skills
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher makes connections and facilitates discussion → Phase 2: Guided connection-making → Phase 3: Independent critical reading → Phase 4: Socially-conscious reading identity
whenNotToUse: When issues might cause distress without proper preparation and support.

subject: ela
name: Speaking and Presentation Skill Development
problemType: Students struggle with formal speaking and presentation
targetMisconception: Belief that speaking ability is a fixed personality trait
teacherMoves: Teach speaking skills explicitly like writing skills (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Build safe environment for speaking growth (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Practice specific speaking skills with feedback
Present with attention to learned skills
fadePlan: Phase 1: Low-stakes speaking with high support → Phase 2: Structured presentations with feedback → Phase 3: Independent presentation planning → Phase 4: Confident speaking identity
whenNotToUse: When anxiety requires additional support before public speaking.

subject: ela
name: Symbolism and Figurative Language Analysis
problemType: Students interpret figurative language literally or miss symbolism
targetMisconception: Belief that texts say exactly what they mean literally
teacherMoves: Teach figurative language and symbolism as meaning-making tools (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with variety of figures and symbols (UDL 8.3)
Connect to author's purpose and effect (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Identify figurative language and potential symbols
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models identification and interpretation → Phase 2: Guided figurative analysis → Phase 3: Independent symbolic interpretation → Phase 4: Sophisticated figurative reading
whenNotToUse: When literal comprehension is the appropriate focus.

subject: ela
name: Text Structure Awareness and Use
problemType: Students don't recognize how text structure affects comprehension
targetMisconception: Belief that all texts are read the same way
teacherMoves: Teach text structures as comprehension tools (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model identifying and using structure for understanding (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Use structure knowledge to predict and comprehend
Apply different reading strategies for different structures
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models structure identification and use → Phase 2: Guided practice with variety → Phase 3: Independent structure awareness → Phase 4: Automatic structure use
whenNotToUse: When text structure is not relevant to comprehension goal.

subject: ela
name: Textual Evidence Selection and Integration
problemType: Students make claims without text support or use evidence without explanation
targetMisconception: Belief that any quote supports any claim or that quoting is the same as analyzing
teacherMoves: Teach evidence as support requiring explanation (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model selecting relevant evidence and connecting to claims (UDL 6.1)
Build from single evidence to multiple evidence arguments (UDL 6.2)
studentTasks: Identify claim that needs evidence support
Select most relevant evidence from text
Embed evidence smoothly with proper attribution
Build arguments with multiple evidence points
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models complete evidence integration → Phase 2: Guided practice with templates → Phase 3: Independent evidence use → Phase 4: Natural evidence-based writing
whenNotToUse: When brainstorming or when textual evidence is not the learning focus.

subject: ela
name: Theme Identification and Development Analysis
problemType: Students identify topics rather than themes or miss theme development
targetMisconception: Belief that themes are explicitly stated rather than developed through text
teacherMoves: Teach theme as developed through text elements (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model tracing theme development across text (UDL 6.1)
Connect theme to author's purpose and technique (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Distinguish topic from theme in texts
Trace how theme develops through plot, character, symbol
Identify textual evidence for theme interpretation
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models with explicit distinction and tracking → Phase 2: Guided theme analysis → Phase 3: Independent theme interpretation → Phase 4: Sophisticated theme analysis
whenNotToUse: When plot comprehension is the primary focus rather than theme.

subject: ela
name: Vocabulary-in-Context Determination Strategy
problemType: Students skip unknown words or rely solely on dictionary
targetMisconception: Belief that vocabulary comes from memorizing definitions rather than context
teacherMoves: Teach context clue types and strategies (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice verifying with dictionary after context guess (UDL 6.2)
studentTasks: Use context clues to make educated guess
Verify guess with dictionary or discussion
Record word with context and meaning
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models with think-aloud → Phase 2: Guided practice with feedback → Phase 3: Independent strategy use → Phase 4: Automatic context-first approach
whenNotToUse: When word meaning is critical to safety or when no context is available.

subject: ela
name: Writer Identity Affirmation and Development
problemType: Students don't see themselves as writers
targetMisconception: Belief that writer identity is for some people but not them
teacherMoves: Provide choice in writing topics and forms (UDL 7.1)
Create community around writing (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Connect writing to student interests and purposes (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Explore personal writing history and preferences
Set personal writing goals aligned with purposes
Engage in regular writing with choice
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher creates writing community with choice → Phase 2: Supported writer identity development → Phase 3: Independent writing life → Phase 4: Lifelong writer identity
whenNotToUse: Never - writer identity should be developed continuously. Adjust choice and support levels.

subject: ela
name: Writing Process Planning and Time Management
problemType: Students rush writing without planning or managing time
targetMisconception: Belief that good writers just sit down and write
teacherMoves: Teach writing as process requiring planning (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Analyze writing task requirements and constraints
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher assigns planning with structured support → Phase 2: Self-selected planning with check-ins → Phase 3: Independent process management → Phase 4: Natural writing process habits
whenNotToUse: When quick writing is appropriate or when timed writing requires different approach.

subject: ela
name: Writing Reflection and Growth Documentation
problemType: Students don't reflect on or track writing development
targetMisconception: Belief that writing ability is fixed rather than growing through practice
teacherMoves: Teach reflection as tool for writing growth (HLP Explicit Instruction)
studentTasks: Identify patterns of strength and growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides reflection with explicit criteria → Phase 2: Regular reflection with prompts → Phase 3: Independent reflective practice → Phase 4: Ongoing reflective writing identity
whenNotToUse: When writing is informal with no skill development focus.
